serves_registry_rows: what a household already has that is on all day and could host (for the energy delta)

sources.name: Residential Energy Consumption Survey, public-use microdata 2020 (v7) and 2024 (v1, preliminary household characteristics)
sources.notice: Source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Residential Energy Consumption Survey 2020 and 2024 public-use microdata. A derived work; not endorsed by the agency.

keys.unit: a household (occupied primary residence), United States
keys.household_size: members, pooled upward where a cell's relative standard error exceeded 7.5 %

envelope.note: a table fitted in 2020 was REFUSED against 2024 for smartphones in one-person households and laptops in the largest: device counts need a year

errors: the agency's jackknife over 60 replicate weights; 'se' is one standard error
declared_not_measured: power state and can-host per kind are declared attributes; the survey does not say which devices are on, and never asks about a router

verdict.twin_phones_per_person_1.0: refused (0.813 per person; 0.999 per adult 18 and over)
verdict.twin_devices_per_person_2.25: certified (2.15 phones, laptops, desktops and tablets)
verdict.scope: the twin's figures are world figures; these verdicts are about the United States

limits: counts differ by building type at equal household size (set-top boxes, desktops, televisions, smart speakers), which this table's rows do not carry; see housing_contrast
have-nots cluster: kinds must not be drawn independently (ratio 2.9)
holds_no_real_feature: no household, person or place; rows of weighted means and shares
